source.title: Mechanistic Failure Modes of Weight Pruning in Transformer Language Models

page_placements.theme: Post-training and compression reconfigure IOI circuits

record.file_problem: none; the provided text includes the paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study removes components by structured weight pruning, then measures IOI behavior and circuit contributions with methods different from the original circuit-discovery evaluation.
record.gate_note: The study applies pruning to GPT-2 Small and reports IOI behavior, DLA, and activation-patching outcomes. The reported GT results concern a different task and circuit, so they are not included as IOI rows. The 300-sentence IOI evaluation uses 15 templates, but the study does not report prompt-variant-specific outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study uses the Wang et al. IOI circuit as a fixed ground truth for auditing 12 pruned GPT-2 small variants. It measures how pruning damages the circuit and behaviour, not whether the circuit explains IOI in GPT-2 small. It does not test faithfulness, completeness or minimality, backup takeover, other models, method dependence of circuit discovery, or prompt variants. The pruned models are altered systems, and pruning removes many non-circuit components at once. So drops in logit difference or DLA cannot show whether the 26-head circuit does IOI (V1), or how circuit-evaluation choices change faithfulness (V5). The reader's V5 link confuses sensitivity of pruning audits (perplexity vs logit difference) with sensitivity of circuit evaluation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors identify two failure modes: magnitude head pruning zeroes the IOI circuit, giving near-chance output, while magnitude neuron pruning at 30% inverts it, giving confident wrong-name predictions with heads intact. Component type matters more than sparsity. A Greater-Than replication shows the critical component type depends on the circuit's architecture. Perplexity and structural checks can miss this damage, so they recommend circuit-level causal analysis for compressed models.
record.recipe_differences: Uses structured weight zeroing of heads or MLP neurons by magnitude or random selection, then measures behavior with IOI logit difference and accuracy and circuit effects with activation patching, path patching, and DLA; it does not reproduce the original circuit-discovery procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: IOI outcomes vary with component type, pruning criterion, and sparsity. The reported behavioral and circuit measures can also give different impressions of damage; prompt-variant-specific sensitivity is not tested.

fits_no_version.finding: Structured pruning of GPT-2 small disrupts the IOI circuit in two modes. Magnitude head pruning (≥50%) zeroes circuit DLA. Magnitude neuron pruning at 30% leaves all 26 heads intact but flips NM/BNM DLA sign (-30.8%, -119.9%), with LD -2.475 and 17.7% accuracy. Perplexity misranks this model as less damaged than random head pruning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compression can zero or invert the IOI circuit's contributions in GPT-2 small while structural and perplexity checks miss the damage.

fits_no_version.finding: The S-INH→NM path is degraded under every pruning condition (path-patching d 0.102–0.365, Table 7). NNM patching d is negative in all twelve conditions (Table 9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: S-Inhibition→Name Mover is the IOI circuit's most pruning-vulnerable pathway.

record.problems: All experiments use GPT-2 small and synthetic IOI prompts; the study does not test natural-language transfer, larger models, or prompt-variant-specific results. No post-pruning weight updates are studied. Uncertainty is not reported for the Table 1 IOI variant values.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted remaining Table 2 DLA entries, most Table 9 activation-patching conditions, Table 7 path-patching results, and Tables 3, 8, and 10 metrics. The kept rows prioritize behavioral outcomes and representative zeroing, inversion, and patching evidence bearing on V1 and V5; the omitted results are mainly further pruning-condition detail or measures not directly named in the claim.

untested.parts: No faithfulness, completeness or minimality test; no knockout of non-circuit components in the intact model. The circuit is taken as given.
No targeted ablation of Name Movers with measurement of backup takeover. Pruning removed NM and BNM together.
GPT-2 small only; no other sizes, models or checkpoints. Greater-Than is a different circuit, not reuse of IOI components.
No comparison of circuit-discovery methods, ablation types or metrics for recovering the circuit.
No variation of ablation, metric or prompt distribution in evaluating circuit faithfulness or completeness.
15 templates are pooled; no results by name order, template or number of names.

record.verdict_notes: The base-model DLA profile (Table 6: NM +3.576, NNM -2.094, BNM +0.427, S-INH +0.384) and base LD 2.942 / 94.8% are qualitatively consistent with the original circuit roles. They are a single descriptive check, not a test of V1's criteria. The reader's V1 label wrongly treats ~46–48% accuracy as non-circuit IOI: with LD below zero, this is chance on a two-name choice. The reader's V5 label rests on pruning-audit metrics, not circuit-evaluation choices. Greater-Than results (L9H1 compensation) concern a different circuit and do not bear on V2.

versions.untested_parts: Does not redo the original faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria as a whole, or knock out everything outside the circuit. It uses pruning, DLA, and patching to assess circuit behavior in pruned models.
No targeted ablation of main Name Mover heads to test whether backup heads take over.
No test of the IOI circuit in other model sizes, checkpoints, or models, or of IOI components being reused for other tasks.
Does not compare circuit-finding methods or alternative ablation types for recovering the same circuit.

Tests different pruning component types, criteria, and sparsities and compares behavioral and circuit measures. It does not compare prompt distributions or alternative circuit-ablation evaluation protocols.
Uses multiple templates and names in an aggregate evaluation, but does not report circuit or behavior results separately by name order, template, or number of names.

relation.reason: Activation patching, path patching and DLA measure damage to the assumed circuit under compression rather than independently testing a claim version.

tranche.reason: Uses the established IOI circuit as ground truth to audit pruning damage. It does not evaluate the catalog's circuit claims or their faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.

source_check.notes: The paper contradicts itself about magnitude neuron selection: Section 3.2 specifies lowest-norm removal, while Sections 4.3 and 4.5 describe largest/highest-weight removal. The checked values and condition labels match its tables.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Pruned GPT-2 Small variants, especially magnitude attention-head pruning at 50% and 70% and magnitude neuron pruning at 30%
reader_labels.reason: Circuit contributions can be zeroed or sign-inverted, while magnitude head pruning leaves 45.7%–47.9% accuracy attributed to non-circuit computation; the original full criteria are not re-tested (r07, r11, r19, r23, r29-r32).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Pruned GPT-2 Small conditions across component type, criterion, sparsity, and reported measures
reader_labels.reason: IOI behavior and class-level contributions vary across pruning choices; for example, magnitude neuron pruning at 30% gives -2.475 mean logit difference while random attention-head pruning at 30% gives -0.706, and the paper reports that perplexity ranks the former as less damaged (r01, r04).
